facts.statement: Fossils of Wendiceratops were discovered in 2010 by fossil prospector Wendy Sloboda in southern Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Its fossils were discovered in 2010 by fossil prospector Wendy Sloboda at the Pinhorn Provincial Grazing Reserve in southern Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: Excavations of Wendiceratops fossils took place between 2011 and 2014.
facts.quote: excavations were carried out from 2011 to 2014

facts.statement: Over 200 fossil specimens of Wendiceratops have been recovered.
facts.quote: More than 200 fossil specimens have been recovered

facts.statement: The Wendiceratops bonebed is considered the oldest evidence that ceratopsians may have lived in herds.
facts.quote: This bonebed is regarded as the oldest evidence of a group of ceratopsians that may have lived together in herds

facts.statement: Paleontologists David Evans and Michael Ryan named and described Wendiceratops pinhornensis in 2015.
facts.quote: In 2015, paleontologists David Evans and Michael Ryan named and described the type species Wendiceratops pinhornensis

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Wendiceratops was found in the Oldman Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, TMP 2011.051.0009, was found in a layer of the Oldman Formation

facts.statement: The holotype of Wendiceratops consists of a single right parietal bone.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a right parietal bone

facts.statement: The mudstone layer containing the fossils is 40 cm thick and dates between 78.7 and 79 million years ago.
facts.quote: The layer of mudstone, 40 cm thick and probably deposited in a single event, has an upper possible age of 79 million years and a lower age of 78.7 million years

facts.statement: A total of 184 specimens representing multiple individuals, including juveniles, were referred to Wendiceratops pinhornensis.
facts.quote: for a total of 184 specimens representing several individuals, including juveniles

facts.statement: Wendiceratops grew to a length of 6 meters and a body mass of 1.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Wendiceratops reached 6 m in length and 1.5 MT in body mass

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Wendiceratops contained at least twenty-six tooth positions.
facts.quote: The maxilla, the upper jaw bone, of Wendiceratops had at least twenty-six tooth positions

facts.statement: A broken nasal horn specimen of Wendiceratops measured 11.5 cm in height and 9 cm in base length.
facts.quote: one broken specimen has a height of 11.5 cm and a base length of 9 cm

facts.statement: Wendiceratops possessed a broad skull frill.
facts.quote: The skull frill of Wendiceratops was broad

facts.statement: The front part of the skull frill was formed by a rectangular squamosal bone.
facts.quote: The front side of the frill was formed by the squamosal bone which had a rectangular shape

facts.statement: The episquamosals on the front of the frill uniquely curled upwards.
facts.quote: Uniquely, they curled upwards

facts.statement: The first epiparietal on the rear frill became tongue-shaped and overhung a large portion of the frill.
facts.quote: This resulted in the first epiparietal becoming tongue-shaped and overhanging a large part of the frill

facts.statement: The ischium of Wendiceratops grew wider toward the lower end, creating a generally rectangular shape.
facts.quote: The ischium of Wendiceratops however, grew wider towards its lower end, resulting in a generally rectangular shape

facts.statement: Wendiceratops is classified in the subfamily Centrosaurinae as a sister species to Sinoceratops.
facts.quote: Wendiceratops was placed in the Centrosaurinae, as a sister species to Sinoceratops

facts.statement: Wendiceratops shared its habitat in the Oldman Formation with dinosaurs including Daspletosaurus, Paronychodon, Troodon, Albertaceratops, and Parasaurolophus.
facts.quote: Being found in the Oldman Formation, Wendiceratops shared its habitat with other dinosaurs such as Daspletosaurus, Paronychodon, Troodon, Albertaceratops, and Parasaurolophus

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the presence of multiple ceratopsid species in the same area was made possible by ecological specializations and high faunal turnover.
facts.quote: They assumed this was made possible by ecological specialisations and also indicated a high faunal turnover, a quick succession of related species

facts.statement: Researchers view the nose horn of Wendiceratops as a transitional form between the low horns of earlier centrosaurines and the taller horns of derived species.
facts.quote: the nose horn of Wendiceratops, erect but probably of moderate size, was by the describing authors seen as a transition between the low horns of earlier forms like Diabloceratops, Nasutoceratops and Albertaceratops and the much taller horns of derived centrosaurines such as Coronosaurus, Centrosaurus and Styracosaurus

facts.statement: It is debated whether the vertical nasal horn of Chasmosaurinae evolved independently in parallel evolution, marking the second time such a horn appeared among ceratopsids.
facts.quote: This would imply that the also long vertical nasal horn of the Chasmosaurinae would have separately been developed in a process of parallel evolution, the second time such a horn would have evolved among the ceratopsids

facts.statement: The genus Wendiceratops was named and described by paleontologists Evans and Ryan in 2015.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Evans & Ryan et al., 2015

facts.statement: Wendiceratops lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 79 to 78 million years ago in the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 79 a 78 millones de años durante el Campaniense

facts.statement: Fossils of Wendiceratops have been found in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: The type specimen was discovered in 2010 by fossil hunter Wendy Sloboda in the Pinhorn Provincial Reserve in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: En 2010, la cazadora canadiense de fósiles Wendy Sloboba halló un yacimiento de huesos fósiles en la reserva provincial Pinhorn al sur del río Milk, condado de Forty Mile No. 8, Alberta, Canadá.

facts.statement: The genus name Wendiceratops honors the fossil hunter Wendy Sloboda and combines it with the Greek term for 'horned face'.
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina la referencia a Wendy Sloboda con el término en griego latinizado ~ceratops, "rostro con cuerno".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Oldman Formation, which dates to the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, TMP 2011.051.0009 fue hallado en una capa de la Formación Oldman, que data del Campaniense.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a single right parietal bone.
facts.quote: El holotipo consiste de un hueso parietal derecho.

facts.statement: Wendiceratops weighed approximately one tonne and measured about 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Wendiceratops pesaba alrededor de una tonelada y tenía una longitud de 6 metros.

facts.statement: No eye horns were found on Wendiceratops.
facts.quote: No se hallaron cuernos oculares.

facts.statement: The nasal bone bears a vertical nasal horn.
facts.quote: El hueso nasal porta un cuerno nasal vertical.

facts.statement: Wendiceratops is distinguished by the lack of a vertical spine on the frill and an erect nasal horn.
facts.quote: Wendiceratops se distingue además por la carencia de una espina vertical en la gola y un cuerno nasal erguido.

facts.statement: The ischium of Wendiceratops has an expanded, rectangular lower end.
facts.quote: El isquion tiene un extremo inferior expandido y de forma rectangular.

facts.statement: Four skin ossifications known as epiesqueamals were attached to the edge of the squamosal bone.
facts.quote: En su borde se sujetaban cuatro osificaciones de la piel u osteodermos, conocidos como los epiescamosales.

facts.statement: Each parietal bone had five epiparietals, conventionally numbered p1 to p5.
facts.quote: Cada parietal tenía cinco, numerados convencionalmente "p1" a "p5".

facts.statement: The fourth and fifth epiparietals, located at the front, resembled the epiesqueamals.
facts.quote: El cuarto y quinto epiparietales, situados al frente, se asemejaban a los epiescamosales.

facts.statement: The first epiparietal acquired a tongue-like shape and extended across much of the frill, pointing slightly outward.
facts.quote: Esto daba como resultado en que el primer epiparietal adquiría una forma de lengua y se extendía por buena parte de la gola, apuntando levemente hacia afuera.

facts.statement: Two large openings called parietal fenestrae are located near the edge of the frill.
facts.quote: Cerca del borde se encuentran dos grandes aberturas, las fenestras parietales.

facts.statement: Wendiceratops belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Wendiceratops is classified within the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: Wendiceratops is positioned as a sister species to Sinoceratops within the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Wendiceratops fue situado en la subfamilia Centrosaurinae, como una especie hermana de Sinoceratops.

facts.statement: Researchers view the erect, moderately sized nasal horn of Wendiceratops as a transitional form between low horns of primitive centrosaurines and the high horns of advanced ones.
facts.quote: El cuerno nasal de Wendiceratops, erguido y probablemente de tamaño moderado, es visto por los autores como una transición entre los cuernos bajos de formas primitivas como Diabloceratops, Nasutoceratops y Albertaceratops y los cuernos mucho más altos de los centrosaurinos avanzados como Coronosaurus, Centrosaurus y Styracosaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the long vertical horn of Chasmosaurinae evolved independently in parallel evolution, potentially being the second time such a horn evolved among ceratopsids.
facts.quote: Esto podría implicar que el largo cuerno vertical de los Chasmosaurinae se habría desarrollado de manera independiente en un proceso de evolución paralela, es decir sería la segunda vez que dicho cuerno evolucionó entre los ceratópsidos.

facts.statement: While each centrosaurine species had a unique frill ornamentation pattern, their postcranial skeletons were highly conservative with little variation.
facts.quote: Si bien cada especie de centrosaurino poseía un patrón único de ornamentación en la gola, su esqueleto postcraneal (su cuerpo tras la cabeza) era muy conservador, ya que mostraba muy poca variación.

facts.statement: Wendiceratops lived alongside predators like Daspletosaurus and herbivores such as Parasaurolophus in the Oldman Formation.
facts.quote: Habiendo sido hallado en la Formación Oldman, Wendiceratops compartía su hábitat con otros dinosaurios como Daspletosaurus, Paronychodon, Troodon, Albertaceratops y Parasaurolophus.

facts.statement: The discovery of Wendiceratops revealed at least five species of ceratopsids in the lower Oldman Formation, including Albertaceratops, Judiceratops, Medusaceratops, and Avaceratops.
facts.quote: Los autores señalaron que tras el descubrimiento de Wendiceratops, ya se conocen no menos de cinco especies de ceratópsidos de la zona inferior de Oldman o las formaciones norteamericanas contemporáneas, incluyendo a Albertaceratops y a Judiceratops, Medusaceratops y Avaceratops.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the coexistence of multiple ceratopsid species was made possible by ecological specializations and indicates a rapid turnover of related species.
facts.quote: Ellos asumen que esto era posible gracias a las especializaciones ecológicas y también indicaban un fuerte recambio faunístico, una rápida sucesión de especies relacionadas.

facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.quote: Type species: Wendiceratops pinhornensis
